Package io.mavlink4j.service

Record Class CapabilityReport

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.mavlink4j.service.CapabilityReport
Record Components:
firmwareVersion - "major.minor.patch", or null for CapabilityReport.Status.NO_REPLY
maturity - the low byte of flight_sw_version — DEV/ALPHA/BETA/RC/OFFICIAL
uid - AUTOPILOT_VERSION.uid — the flight-controller hardware uid, useful for detecting a board swap (a changed uid on the same system id); null for CapabilityReport.Status.NO_REPLY
raw - the whole message, for a caller that needs a field this record omits; null for CapabilityReport.Status.NO_REPLY

Thread-safety: Immutable and thread-safe, apart from the raw message the caller must not mutate.

public record CapabilityReport(CapabilityReport.Status status, String firmwareVersion, CapabilityReport.Maturity maturity, Set<io.dronefleet.mavlink.common.MavProtocolCapability> capabilities, long boardVersion, int vendorId, int productId, BigInteger uid, io.dronefleet.mavlink.common.AutopilotVersion raw) extends Record
What a vehicle answered to MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE(AUTOPILOT_VERSION) — decoded far enough to be useful, and no further.

The two decodings live here rather than in every caller because both are easy to get wrong: flight_sw_version is a packed uint32, not a number anyone should print raw, and capabilities is a bitmask whose set bits are the aircraft's own claim about which protocols it speaks. Turning those into a version string and a flag set is protocol knowledge and belongs at this layer; deciding what they mean for a feature ("can this aircraft fly a mission?") is domain policy and deliberately does not.
